findings.title: Migration crashes when the embed_category / uncategorized_category_id rows are missing
findings.body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` is called on the result of a join between `categories` and the `embed_category` site setting. When that setting was never saved (the default was '', so the row is normally absent) or matches no category, `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The same applies to `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value']` when that row doesn't exist, as on a fresh DB. Most installs have no `embed_category` row, so the migration fails for them. Guard against empty results (`.first`, `cmd_tuples`).

findings.title: Raw string interpolation of host values into INSERT SQL
findings.body: Each host line from the old site setting is interpolated straight into the SQL string. A value containing a single quote breaks the migration and is an injection vector. Lines can also contain `\r` or whitespace and are not stripped. Use `quote`/`connection.quote` or ActiveRecord to insert, and strip each line. Also, the old `type: host_list` values could include `http://` and paths, which are only normalized later by the model callbacks and not here.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on nil host and mutates input in place
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil. The controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, which is nil if the param is omitted, so this causes a 500 instead of a validation error. `sub!` also mutates the string in place, which can alter the caller's or params' string. Use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`, or guard on `host.present?`.

findings.title: Case-insensitive lookup only lowercases the column, not the input
findings.body: The query is `lower(host) = ?` with `uri.host` unmodified. A referer or embed URL with uppercase letters in the host (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/...`) will not match a stored host, so legitimate embeds are rejected. Downcase the parameter too. The method also returns `false` or a record, which is an inconsistent return type.

findings.title: update/destroy do not handle a missing record
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id, and `save_host(nil)` / `host.destroy` then raise NoMethodError (500). Use `find` or return a 404. `params[:embeddable_host]` being absent likewise raises in `save_host`.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains the `:embeddable_host` fabricator. All the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. They work only because all fabricator files are loaded, but anyone looking for them in the conventional file will not find them, and the diff is misleading. Restore the original category fabricator and put only the embeddable host one in its own file.

findings.title: Category shown after save may not match what the server stored
findings.body: After save, the category is set locally from `this.get('categoryId')`. When the user leaves the chooser empty, the server substitutes the uncategorized category, but the client sets `category` to `findById(null)` (undefined). The row then renders a blank category badge until reload. Use the `category_id` from the server response. In the same save path, the `edit` action seeds `categoryId` from `host.category.id` and the new-host path leaves it null.

findings.title: Hydrated *_ids arrays can contain undefined and `|| []` is dead code
findings.body: `obj[k].map(...)` returns an array that may contain `undefined` entries when a sub-record isn't in the root collection. `hydrated || []` is always truthy, so the fallback never applies, and consumers get undefined elements. Filter out missing entries. The branch also assumes `obj[k]` is an array without checking.

findings.title: Test no longer tests what its name says
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks embeddable hosts, but the test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' remains. It passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false. The nested `describe` also calls `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` even though the host is irrelevant to the result. The test is misleading and should be removed or rewritten.

findings.title: New admin controllers have no behavioural tests
findings.body: Both new admin controller specs only assert the class inherits from AdminController. Nothing covers create/update/destroy, the default-category fallback, validation errors, non-admin access, or the embedding show endpoint. The nil-record and nil-host failure paths therefore go untested. The migration is untested too.
